key_insight: There is a clear trade-off between latent-space compactness and long-horizon forecast reliability: nonlinear autoencoders compress better, but POD produces smoother latent dynamics that are easier to predict stably.
engineering_relevance: For real-time flow control, the most compact reduced-order model is not necessarily the best; predictive stability may matter more than maximum reconstruction fidelity for MPC and reinforcement learning.
method: Compared POD with convolutional autoencoders and two variational autoencoders for spatial compression.
Used LSTM-based temporal predictors to forecast latent dynamics in two controlled 2D wake cases.
Assessed both short-term reconstruction quality and long-horizon forecast stability/divergence.
evidence_signal: Across a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball, CAEs gave sharper short-term reconstructions but more irregular broadband latent trajectories, while POD yielded smoother trajectories and more reliable long-horizon predictions.
watch_item: Higher compression can increase forecast instability and catastrophic divergence, so encoder choice should be validated on prediction horizon and control robustness, not only reconstruction error.
paper_title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
